description: Computer Science Team Have passion To Develop A Software Solution To Nasa Problems
summary:
DELTA 2100 — The Last Line of Defense is an interactive environmental risk intelligence platform built for NASA’s Earth System Trend Detective challenge. Coastal regions and river deltas face growing threats from sea-level rise, land subsidence, erosion, and flooding, but the information about them is scattered across many sources. DELTA 2100 brings it together in three connected experiences:

The Past – Disaster Archive: Explore real locations hit by severe environmental disasters, land loss, or displacement, and learn what happened, why, and how communities were affected.
The Present & Future – Risk Intelligence: Investigate five vulnerable regions: the Nile Delta, Ganges–Brahmaputra Delta, Mississippi Delta, Venice, and the Maldives. Use satellite imagery, environmental indicators, and regional risk data to see how these areas are changing and to visualize possible scenarios toward 2100.
The Future – Survival Simulation: Play an interactive game, make decisions, and test protective strategies to see how today’s actions shape tomorrow’s outcomes.

By linking historical evidence, environmental trends, and future scenarios in one accessible platform, DELTA 2100 helps people understand these risks and the importance of acting before it is too late.
details:
DELTA 2100 — Project Details

1. What Does DELTA 2100 Do?

DELTA 2100 is an interactive climate-risk intelligence and environmental awareness platform designed to explore how climate change is reshaping vulnerable coastal regions and river deltas around the world.

The platform focuses on three interconnected experiences that transform environmental information into meaningful, accessible insights.

1. Disaster Archive — When Nature Changes Everything

This section documents real-world environmental disasters and disappearing or severely affected locations. Users can explore historical events, discover the environmental factors behind them, and compare before-and-after imagery to understand how landscapes and communities have changed over time.

Rather than presenting climate change as abstract statistics, this archive connects scientific and environmental changes to real places, real events, and their human consequences.

2. Risk Intelligence — Explore the Threat

This section allows users to explore five vulnerable geographical regions and understand the environmental threats they face.

It focuses on key factors such as sea-level rise, coastal erosion, land subsidence, extreme rainfall, and flooding. Through geographical visualization and environmental indicators, users can explore why these locations are vulnerable and how climate-related pressures may affect their future.

3. LAST 100 YEARS — A Survival Simulation

This interactive experience places users in the role of decision-makers responsible for protecting vulnerable communities.

Users explore possible future scenarios, make strategic decisions, and allocate limited resources between different adaptation and protection strategies. The simulation demonstrates how decisions made today can influence the resilience of communities over time.

The experience is designed to make long-term environmental challenges understandable through interaction, exploration, and decision-making.

2. Benefits and Intended Impact

DELTA 2100 aims to:

  • Raise awareness of the environmental threats facing coastal communities and river deltas.
  • Make historical environmental disasters easier to understand through visual storytelling.
  • Help users explore geographical vulnerability and climate-related risks.
  • Demonstrate the importance of early preparation and climate adaptation.
  • Encourage informed decision-making through interactive future scenarios.
  • Make Earth observation and environmental information more accessible to students, researchers, educators, and the public.

Our ultimate goal is to bridge the gap between environmental data and public understanding, transforming complex scientific information into an experience that encourages awareness, preparedness, and action.

3. Technology and Development

The platform is developed as a web-based interactive experience.

The development work includes:

  • Frontend: Web technologies for building the user interface and interactive experiences.
  • Backend: Node.js and Express.js for server-side logic and API development.
  • Database: MongoDB for managing and organizing application data.
  • Data Visualization: Interactive geographical and environmental visualizations.
  • Deployment: Web-based deployment to make the platform accessible online.

The architecture is designed to support the integration of Earth observation datasets, geographical information, historical records, and future scenario simulations.

4. Creativity and Innovation

DELTA 2100 combines three approaches that are often presented separately: historical environmental storytelling, geographical risk exploration, and interactive future decision-making.

Its creative strength lies in connecting the past, present, and possible future within one experience.

Users do not simply read about climate change. They explore places that have already experienced environmental disasters, investigate locations facing growing risks, and experience the consequences of strategic decisions through simulation.

By combining scientific context, visual storytelling, geographical exploration, and interactive decision-making, DELTA 2100 turns a complex global challenge into an engaging and understandable experience.

5. Factors Considered

The project considers:

  • Environmental vulnerability and geographical differences between regions.
  • The relationship between sea-level rise, erosion, subsidence, and flooding.
  • The human, ecological, agricultural, and infrastructural consequences of environmental change.
  • The importance of reliable scientific sources and transparent data attribution.
  • The accessibility of environmental information to non-specialist audiences.
  • The uncertainty of long-term climate scenarios and the need to communicate possible futures rather than guaranteed predictions.

DELTA 2100 is built around one central idea:

The future of vulnerable communities should not be discovered only after it is too late.
